chunks: And it is narrated from Hassan al-Jammal, who said:

I carried Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) from Medina to Mecca. When we reached the Mosque of Ghadir, he looked at the left side of the mosque and said, 'That is the spot of the foot of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), where he said, "Whomever I am his master, Ali is his master."'

Then he looked to the other side and said, 'That is the spot where the tents of the hypocrites were pitched, including those of Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. When they saw him raising his hand, some of them said, "Look at his eyes—they are turning as if he is mad."

Then Archangel Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with this verse: "Indeed, those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their glances when they hear the message, and they say, 'He is indeed mad.' But it is nothing except a reminder for the worlds."

key_terms.الذِّكْرَ: The message/remembrance (referring to the Quranic revelation or announcement)
key_terms.الْغَدِيرِ: Ghadir (a place near Mecca, site of the Prophet's declaration)
key_terms.مَوْلاَهُ: His master/leader (referring to the concept of Wilayah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Mosque of Ghadir in Shia tradition regarding the declaration of Imam Ali's authority?
ai.summary: This narration from Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih highlights the Ghadir Mosque as a sacred site of Wilayah, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) pinpointed the exact location of the Prophet’s declaration and the subsequent reaction of the hypocrites. It provides a unique exegetical link between the physical act of raising the hand during the announcement and the Quranic description of the disbelievers' gaze in Surah Al-Qalam, interpreting their accusation of madness as a response to the spiritual intensity of the event.
